'''Stuart Andrew West''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is an evolutionary biologist studying [[Sociobiology|social evolution]] and a Professor of [[evolutionary biology]] in the [[Biology]] Department at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=biology>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603225606/https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/people/stuart-west|archivedate=2024-06-03|url=https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/people/stuart-west|title=Professor Stuart West|website=biology.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080906195332/http://westgroup.biology.ed.ac.uk/media.html|archivedate=2008-09-06|url=http://westgroup.biology.ed.ac.uk/media.html|title=Staurt West|website=westgroup.biology.ed.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The West Group|url=http://www.zoo.ox.ac.uk/group/west|website=zoo.ox.ac.uk|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121117173844/http://www.zoo.ox.ac.uk/group/west|archivedate=2012-11-17}}</ref>

==Education==
West completed the [[Natural Sciences Tripos]] as an undergraduate student at the [[University of Cambridge]]<ref name=orcid>Stuart A. West {{ORCID}}</ref> followed by a [[PhD]] at [[Imperial College London]] on [[reproduction|reproductive strategies]] in parasitic [[hymenoptera]].<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|first=Stuart Andrew|last=West|oclc=940354334|id={{ProQuest| 1780576736}}|url=https://search.libraries.london.ac.uk/permalink/44SHL_INST/1rfg6e9/alma991021988249709266|website=london.ac.uk|year=1995|publisher=Imperial College London|title=Reproductive strategies in parasitic hymenoptera}}</ref><ref name=royale>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/stuart-west-10844/|website=royalsociety.org|title=Professor Stuart West FRS}}</ref>

==Career and research==
West's primary research interests are in the area of social evolution, [[sex allocation]] theory and [[evolution|microbial evolution]]. His research has attracted media attention,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zoo.ox.ac.uk/group/west/media.html|title= Media|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014021123/http://www.zoo.ox.ac.uk/group/west/media.html|archivedate=2017-10-14}}</ref> and has been published in high profile journals such as ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'',<ref name=nature>{{cite q| Q53557688}}</ref> ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'',<ref name=science>{{cite q| Q34589033}}</ref> the ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]''<ref name=pnas>{{cite q| Q28608544}}</ref> and ''[[Current Biology]]''.<ref name=current>{{cite q| Q34666546 }}</ref><ref name=gs/><ref name=epmc/><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref> West uses theoretical and empirical approaches to explain the evolution of cooperation, communication, and [[sex ratio]].<ref name=social>{{cite q| Q34575748}}</ref>

With  with [[John Krebs, Baron Krebs|John Krebs]] and [[Nicholas Barry Davies|Nicholas Davies]], West is the co-author of the textbook ''An Introduction to Behavioural Ecology''.<ref name=evbook>{{cite book|title=An Introduction to Behavioural Ecology|first1=Nicholas B. |last1=Davies|authorlink1=Nicholas Barry Davies|first2=John R. |last2=Krebs |authorlink2=John Krebs, Baron Krebs|first3= Stuart A. |last3=West |ISBN=9781444398472|oclc=898271534|edition=4th|year=2014|publisher=[[Wiley Blackwell]]}}</ref> 

===Awards and honours===
West was a distinguished junior scholar in residence at the [[Peter Wall Institute for Advanced Studies]], [[University of British Columbia]], Canada in 1999 and he has won the [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] for Zoology (2006), the Scientific Medal of the [[Zoological Society of London]] (2006)<ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207023858/http://websiterepository.ed.ac.uk/news/060804chancellorawards.html|archivedate=2022-12-07|url=http://websiterepository.ed.ac.uk/news/060804chancellorawards.html|title=News & Events - Academic Innovators to Accept Awards at Royal Dinner|website=ed.ac.uk}}</ref>. He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2026.<ref name=frs>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-27 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/ |access-date=2026-05-31 |website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2026 |language=en}}</ref> He is a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO)<ref name=embo>{{cite web|url=https://people.embo.org/profile/stuart-a-west|website=people.embo.org|publisher=[[European Molecular Biology Organization]]|location=Heidelberg|title=Stuart A. West|author=Anon|year=2014}}</ref> and a former{{when|date=June 2026}} holder of a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]].<ref name=royale/> He was awarded an [[List of Ig Nobel Prize winners#2026|Ig Nobel Prize]] in 2026, alongside fellow Oxford researcher Matilda Brindle and University of Florida researcher Catherine F. Talbot, for their work on reconstructing the evolutionary history of human kissing.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ramakrishman |first1=Adithi |title=Scientists studying cockroach milk and nose-blowing win Ig Nobel prizes for quirky science |url=https://www.latimes.com/science/story/2026-09-05/research-on-cockroach-milk-nose-blowing-wins-ig-nobel-prizes |access-date=6 September 2026 |work=Los Angeles Times |agency=AP News |date=5 September 2026}}</ref>
